newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOWLER HEADS LAST-GASP WINNER FOR LIVERPOOL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOWLER HEADS LAST-GASP WINNER FOR LIVERPOOL.

text.p: Robbie Fowler headed a 90th minute goal for Liverpool to snatch a 4-3 premier league win over Newcastle in a pulsating climax at Anfield on Monday.
Liverpool, having seemingly thrown away victory by squandering a 3-0 lead in 17 second-half minutes, are now second in the table, just one point behind leaders and champions Manchester United.
The breathtaking finale mirrored the corresponding fixture last season when Stan Colleymore gave Liverpool a 4-3 win by scoring in the final moments.
This time Liverpool were moving with utter certainty to an emphatic victory when they led 3-0 midway through the second half.
Keith Gillespie pulled a goal back after 71 minutes but Liverpool still appeared set for a convincing win, until Newcastle scored twice in a minute.
Colombian Faustino Asprilla lobbed goalkeeper David James in the 87th minute and Warren Barton equalised in the 88th.
But in the dramatic final seconds, Norwegian defender Stig Inge Bjornebye sent over a cross from the left and Fowler rose to head the winner.
It was a heartbreaking result for former Liverpool player and manager Kenny Dalglish, making his first trip back to Anfield since becoming Newcastle's manager in January.
He was made to pay for an ultra-defensive opening gambit when he played with an unadventurous 5-4-1 formation in which Asprilla was an isolated figure up front.

Liverpool seized the lead after 29 minutes through a classic strike from Steve McManaman, who curled the ball home from the edge of the box with goalkeeper Shaka Hislop grasping at air as the ball nestled in the net.
A minute later Czech Patrik Berger scored his first league goal since September when he followed up a Fowler shot that bounced back off a post to ram the loose ball home.

Fowler then scored a superb oportunist goal in the 43rd minute when he collected a long through ball from Jamie Redknapp, nipping in between Hislop and Belgian defender Philippe Albert, who were left sitting on their backsides and looking at each other in disbelief as Fowler planted the ball in the empty net.
Newcastle badly missed their injured 15 million pounds ($24 million) England striker Alan Shearer and, to all intents and purposes, his eight million pounds strike partner Les Ferdinand.

Ferdinand came on as a substitute after halftime but lasted only 10 minutes before walking disconsolately off still clearly suffering with the hamstring injury that stopped him playing in the first place.

Liverpool, whose title chances seemeed to have disappeared after their 1-0 defeat at Aston Villa on March 2, found themselves right back in the hunt on Saturday after leaders Manchester United surprisingly lost 2-1 at Sunderland.

The victory over Newcastle moved Liverpool into second place on 56 points, one point behind Manchester United, and if manager Roy Evans' team win all their remaining mathes -- including the home match with United on April 19 -- no other team can catch them.
